overview.headline: Drag force expressed through coefficient density velocity and reference area

keyPoints.point: Drag dependence includes density of air and velocity squared plus viscosity and compressibility and shape and inclination
keyPoints.quote: depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity

keyPoints.point: Drag equation sets drag equal to coefficient times density times half velocity squared times reference area
keyPoints.quote: drag D is equal to the drag coefficient Cd times the density rho (ρ) times half of the velocity V squared times the reference area A

keyPoints.point: Drag coefficient includes form drag skin friction drag wave drag and induced drag components
keyPoints.quote: The drag coefficient given above includes form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag, and induced drag components.

keyPoints.point: Reference area given in drag equation is given as reference area and may be wing or frontal or total surface area
keyPoints.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyTerms.gloss: single variable that collects complex dependencies into one value for drag
keyTerms.quote: For drag, this variable is called the drag coefficient, designated “Cd.”

keyTerms.gloss: area used to characterize aerodynamic force and to convert coefficient values
keyTerms.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyTerms.gloss: pressure term called dynamic pressure that appears in Bernoulli relation
keyTerms.quote: is called the dynamic pressure and appears in Bernoulli’s pressure equation.

keyTerms.gloss: property designated by rho that scales with velocity squared to give pressure
keyTerms.quote: In the equation given above, the density is designated by the letter rho (ρ).
